1238.skill_name: Discuss and list early warning signs of relapse
1238.skill_description: Jointly discussing the client's relapse markers with the client, concretizing early signs and forming a checklist, for timely identification and self-monitoring after termination, including emotional, behavioral and physiological cues, clarifying when it is considered needing to initiate coping.
1238.when_to_use: At the outlook part of the termination phase, when starting to discuss the identification and self-monitoring arrangements for Symptom relapse.
1238.trigger: The client mentions 'I might relapse again' or 'there has been some resurgence lately', or shows verbal/behavioral signals of mild old symptoms while still able to maintain functioning.

1239.skill_description: Based on techniques already mastered in counseling, developing concrete operational steps for relapse, such as behavioral activation for depression, exposure for Anxiety, and clarifying execution order and frequency, ensuring the client can follow the list when relapsing.
1239.when_to_use: After relapse signs have been clarified, in the closing stage, formulating a relapse-response action plan and homework.
1239.trigger: When the client says 'I do not know what to do when relapsing' or 'need specific steps', or asks how to apply learned techniques.

1240.skill_name: Announce Consolidation sessions and early help-seeking standards
1240.skill_description: Announcing 1—3 Consolidation session times (about 3, 6, 12 months), agreeing on standards and channels for contacting early when relapse occurs and self-help is ineffective, clarifying appointment procedures, reducing the helplessness of coping alone.
1240.when_to_use: At the arrangement and safety plan segment before the end, when consolidating subsequent support and help-seeking procedures.
1240.trigger: When the client feels uneasy about coping alone after termination, worries about relapse without support, or asks about follow-up contact arrangements.

1241.skill_name: Repeated situational rehearsal and automatic-thought correction
1241.skill_description: Guiding the client to rehearse illness-worsening scenarios, identifying and handling Automatic thoughts during recurrence, practicing self-reminders like 'this is normal, temporary', to reduce panic and maintain continued coping and practice.
1241.when_to_use: When the client has improved and needs to mentally prepare for possible relapse and train cognitive coping.
1241.trigger: When the client still worries the future will be worse during improvement, viewing fluctuations as failure, or describing catastrophizing Automatic thoughts.

1242.skill_description: Make a 'relapse coping card' with the client, listing the steps and specific techniques for self-help first and noting when to switch to seeking help; a guide to keep at hand for checking and rapidly executing in case of relapse after the counseling ends.
1242.when_to_use: At the closing of the session, implements concrete tools and portable reminders for quick execution at relapse.
1242.trigger: The client easily panics or forgets at relapse, asking for a guide clear at a glance, or hoping for portable reminders.

1254.skill_description: Jointly sorts out and lists with the client the signs and warning signals of symptom relapse, defines what counts as relapse manifestations, so they can perceive in time at an early stage and start coping plans accordingly.
1254.when_to_use: At the outlook phase of the closing session or in Consolidation sessions, when developing relapse prevention and coping plans; can also supplement and improve when reviewing recent fluctuations.
1254.trigger: When the client worries 'will it relapse', or describes recent symptom resurgence but is unsure whether it counts as relapse, hard to distinguish warning signals.

1255.skill_description: Agreeing with the client that once relapse manifestations appear, immediately deploying techniques learned in treatment (such as behavioral activation for depression, exposure for Anxiety), and persisting in daily scenarios.
1255.when_to_use: When formulating the relapse coping plan; or when the client reports that early signs of relapse have appeared and operational guidance for 'what to do right now' needs to be concretized.
1255.trigger: When the client shows or reports typical resurgence symptoms (such as Low mood, avoidance, insomnia, palpitations), and asks 'what to do/which trick to use'.

1256.skill_description: Guiding the client to rehearse illness-worsening scenarios, identifying and correcting Automatic thoughts, practicing replacing catastrophizing with self-cues like 'this is normal, temporary', reducing relapse Anxiety.
1256.when_to_use: When nearing termination or in Consolidation sessions, for psychologically preparing for relapse and reinforcing self-regulation; also for individuals with obvious separation Anxiety.
1256.trigger: When the client feels uneasy about termination, using catastrophic language like 'back to square one' or 'it is over', or repeatedly worrying fluctuations are uncontrollable.

1257.skill_description: Urges the making of a 'coping card', writing the concrete steps and technique list for when relapse occurs, available to carry; agrees that before contacting the counselor, first try to cope independently following the card's process.
1257.when_to_use: At the skill consolidation and tool configuration phase before termination; when reviewing tool use and updating entries in Consolidation sessions.
1257.trigger: When the client says they would be at a loss when relapsing, easily panicked, or tends to seek external comfort and guidance first.

1258.skill_name: Announce Consolidation sessions and early follow-up visits
1258.skill_description: Pre-arranging 1—3 Consolidation session time points (about 3/6/12 months), and clarifying that if self-help is ineffective or symptoms worsen, follow-up visits can be scheduled early, obtaining timely support and Intervention.
1258.when_to_use: Used in the planning stage of ending counseling, when discussing follow-up support and risk channels; or before case closing for cases with higher relapse risk.
1258.trigger: When the client expresses needing follow-up support, worrying independent coping is insufficient, or relapse has occurred with limited self-help strategy effects.

1259.skill_name: Self-therapy sessions to cope with relapse
1259.skill_description: Teaching and requiring the use of self-therapy session checklists (such as Thought record sheet) when relapsing or fluctuating to independently sort problems, hypotheses and action plans, reinforcing continued self-help ability.
1259.when_to_use: During the self-help ability training and consolidation phase before termination; home self-help handling when relapse occurs but visiting is temporarily inconvenient.
1259.trigger: When the client says Being alone easily leads to losing control, not knowing how to respond step by step, or hoping for a concrete self-help process to follow.

1243.skill_name: Discuss applying learned techniques to new problems
1243.skill_description: In the closing session, discuss the newly emerged difficulties one by one with the client, select and transfer the cognitive and behavioral techniques learned in counseling, and formulate concrete application steps and practice arrangements.
1243.when_to_use: In the outlook segment of the ending stage, the goal is to establish operable coping plans for new problems; the client is willing to consolidate and extend the gains of the counseling.
1243.trigger: When the client raises recent or possible new situations and challenges, or expresses worries and uncertainty about not knowing how to cope when encountering New problems.

1244.skill_name: Extend counseling gains to other life domains
1244.skill_description: Guiding the client to extend gains from the current problem to other life domains, identifying transferable skills, and discussing specific application methods and directions in different situations.
1244.when_to_use: When reviewing and discussing gains at the termination phase, aiming to extend learning to other areas of future life to address potential new challenges.
1244.trigger: The client focuses the gains only on the improvement of the current problem, or asks whether these methods can be applied to other relationship, work or life situations.

1245.skill_name: Let the client lead the agenda and homework in preparation for new problems
1245.skill_description: Gradually having the client lead the agenda and assign homework in sessions, practicing independent use of learned cognitive and behavioral techniques, laying the foundation for autonomously handling New problems after termination.
1245.when_to_use: In the several sessions before the ending, the goal is to improve self-efficacy and the ability of independent application, preparing to face all kinds of new problems after the ending.
1245.trigger: When the client overly relies on the counselor's arrangements and decisions in sessions, or shows hesitant, unconfident words and behaviors about independently applying techniques.

1227.skill_description: Jointly sorting with the client 'what was done' that brought improvement, Questioning focusing on specific cognitive adjustments and behavioral attempts, forming a clear causal chain, avoiding vague generalizations, to facilitate future repeated application.
1227.when_to_use: In the counseling-effect evaluation at the end of a session - the segment of reviewing the counseling process, when entering 'summarizing successful experiences and insights', used to make progress concrete.
1227.trigger: The client only says 'I feel better' and 'there is improvement', having difficulty pointing out concrete changes or practices; the narrative stays at the emotional level and lacks action details.

1228.skill_name: Prompting the client to distill personal takeaways
1228.skill_description: Through open Questioning, inviting them to summarize insights and experiences in counseling, encouraging using their own language to distill transferable principles and strategies, forming memorable key takeaways.
1228.when_to_use: In the 'summarize successful experiences and insights' segment of the ending session, used to sublimate the client's feelings into reusable experience and principles.
1228.trigger: When the client spontaneously says 'learned a lot' or 'have some insights', but expresses vaguely, not yet able to distill key points, or stays at scattered fragments.

1229.skill_name: Emphasize key points of cognitive and behavioral change
1229.skill_description: After the client summarizes, point out from the side the key mechanisms of change, highlight the role of cognitive restructuring and behavioral practice in improving emotions and functioning, helping consolidate correct understanding and application.
1229.when_to_use: At the review and summary stage, after the client has described progress and realizations, used to frame the key factors and connect them to CBT principles.
1229.trigger: When the client's summary does not yet touch on 'cognitive change'/'behavioral change', or confuses the causes of change; saying improvement was accidental or due to external factors.

1230.skill_name: Assign pre-session review of counseling notes
1230.skill_description: Before the formal summary, arranging homework, requiring the client to review counseling notes, reviewing the journey and gains, thinking about key gains in advance, to deepen summaries, improve effects and reinforce self-efficacy.
1230.when_to_use: At the preparation stage before ending the session or at the start of the last few sessions, used to prepare for 'summarizing successful experiences and realizations'.
1230.trigger: About to enter the closing summary while the client appears at a loss or the content is scattered; the memory of the gains from counseling is vague, needing a structured review in order to summarize.

1234.skill_name: Discussing applying learned methods to residual symptoms and clarifying self-treatment
1234.skill_description: When ending the session, guide the client, with regard to the remaining problems and symptoms, to discuss how to continue using the methods learned in the counseling to cope, and clarify the self-therapy work and tasks that need to be continued.
1234.when_to_use: At the outlook segment of the closing session phase, when identifying unfinished issues; when the treatment course is normally completed or terminated but symptoms remain.
1234.trigger: When the client indicates some symptoms remain before termination (such as Anxiety not yet fully gone), or worries about still struggling to cope with these problems after leaving counseling.

1235.skill_name: Continuously applying learned techniques and self-assigning homework until symptoms are eliminated
1235.skill_description: Urging the client to continue the technical methods used during sessions (such as Exposure techniques for Anxiety), arranging and executing Homework on their own, continuing practice until all Residual symptoms are eliminated.
1235.when_to_use: When formulating future Coping strategies at the closing session; when Residual symptoms exist and continuation practice plans need concretizing.
1235.trigger: When the client still reports specific residual symptoms (such as 'still some Anxiety'), and asks or shows uncertainty about how to continue practicing and consolidating.

1236.skill_name: Letting the client lead the agenda and homework to independently handle residual symptoms
1236.skill_description: Before termination, gradually shifting to the client leading the session process, including agenda setting, homework assignment and cognitive technique application training, to reinforce their ability to independently handle residual problems.
1236.when_to_use: At the ending stage or when session frequency gradually decreases, to raise the client's autonomy and confidence in facing residual symptoms after ending.
1236.trigger: The client is highly dependent on the counselor's arrangements and hesitant about self-assigned tasks, or is about to enter the stage of reduced session frequency and termination.

1237.skill_name: Guiding self-therapy sessions to handle residual problems per the standard checklist
1237.skill_description: Teaches and assigns self-treatment sessions, letting the client regularly handle residual symptoms and difficulties by themself according to standard question lists (such as the thought record form), continuing the treatment effect.
1237.when_to_use: When regular sessions gradually decrease or are about to end, for consolidating skills and preparing for continued self-help handling of residual problems after termination.
1237.trigger: The client begins to improve, sessions decrease in frequency or will end, and expresses hope for a structured method to keep coping with problems after ending.

1217.skill_name: Guide review of the initial state and stage-wise changes
1217.skill_description: Systematically review with the client the state changes from the first visit to now, sorting out stage by stage problem improvement, efforts made, and key turning points, forming an overall assessment of symptom and functioning improvement, and clarifying the current health level and progress trajectory.
1217.when_to_use: In the 'counseling effect evaluation' step of ending counseling, carrying out the review part, used to compare the initial and current states and comprehensively assess the degree of improvement and functional recovery.
1217.trigger: When describing current life and symptoms, the client mentions 'much better than when I first came' or 'still some distress', expressing attention to or puzzlement about their own changes.

1218.skill_name: Assign review homework to improve summary quality
1218.skill_description: Before the formal summary, require the client to review counseling notes, review the course, and self-evaluate the gains, so they enter the session with organized material, improving the depth and accuracy of the evaluation.
1218.when_to_use: When the ending stage begins to prepare the summary or the last few sessions are arranged, in preparation for review and effect evaluation.
1218.trigger: When the client says they are not sure what they learned, memory is vague or they have difficulty specifically describing progress and key events.

1219.skill_name: Identify and discuss Residual symptoms to formulate a self-treatment plan
1219.skill_description: Define with the client the remaining symptoms and functional limitations, discuss continued application of the methods and techniques learned in counseling, and arrange ongoing homework as a self-treatment plan after termination.
1219.when_to_use: At the outlook part of the closing session, assessing Residual symptoms for 'problems not yet concluded' and formulating follow-up plans.
1219.trigger: When the client reports Anxiety, lowness or behavioral distress intermittently appearing, or admits some symptoms are not yet fully eliminated.

1220.skill_name: Clarify relapse signs and develop coping plans
1220.skill_description: Jointly identifying possible early markers of Symptom relapse, listing specific coping techniques and steps during relapse, so the client can timely notice and self-handle after termination.
1220.when_to_use: Used in the outlook and coping strategy discussion of the ending session, especially to formulate contingency plans for clients with relapse risk.
1220.trigger: When the client expresses worries about future illness recurrence, or recent symptoms fluctuate with worries of 'getting worse again'.

1221.skill_name: Announce and schedule Consolidation session follow-up milestones
1221.skill_description: Informing that 1 to 3 Consolidation sessions will be arranged after termination, recommending the first at 3 months, the second at 6 months, the third at one year; follow-up can be advanced if relapse occurs, establishing a timeline for subsequent assessment and support.
1221.when_to_use: When nearing termination, for planning follow-up and support, relieving separation Anxiety and setting health monitoring milestones.
1221.trigger: When the client feels uneasy about facing problems independently, asks about follow-up support or follow-up arrangements, or worries about being unable to effectively handle relapse.

1231.skill_name: Frame counseling gains as growth, focusing on ability improvement
1231.skill_description: Guiding the shift of Gains from counseling from solving a single problem to Personal growth and ability improvement, specifically pointing out changes in core abilities like handling relationships, emotion regulation, and taking these as the main outcomes.
1231.when_to_use: At the review-Gains from counseling phase of the closing session or Consolidation session, when results need summarizing and gains enhanced; the client cooperates but focuses on effectiveness.
1231.trigger: When the client emphasizes 'the problem is solved/not solved', talking little about their own ability changes; defining success only as the resolution of the current dilemma.

1232.skill_name: Guide the client to review and name learned skills
1232.skill_description: Inviting the client to systematically take stock and name learned methods and tools, such as perspective-taking, positive Interpretation, etc.; recording skills as a checklist, reinforcing memory and future transferable use.
1232.when_to_use: At the gains-summary phase of the closing session, aiming to consolidate methods and tools, forming a skill checklist that can be called upon anytime.
1232.trigger: When the client describes learned methods vaguely or says 'do not remember well'/'just feeling better', unable to specifically list or name.

1233.skill_name: Promote generalization of counseling gains to other areas
1233.skill_description: Discusses with the client expanding the learned methods to scenes such as friends and colleagues outside marriage, jointly designs transfer situations and application plans, promoting sustained use across domains.
1233.when_to_use: At the review-follow-up and outlook segment of the closing session or Consolidation session, aiming to extend gains to broader life and interpersonal scenarios.
1233.trigger: When the client only talks about application in a single relationship or situation, expressing 'mainly used in marital problems', not yet considering other areas.

1222.skill_name: Guide recall of the initial state and problem baseline
1222.skill_description: Guide the client to describe in specific detail the situation at the time of their first consultation, the intensity of the symptoms and the functional impairment and the goals then, establishing a comparable baseline providing a clear reference point for staged reviews later.
1222.when_to_use: At the starting stage of the review step of the closing session, used to open a systematic review and establish a starting point.
1222.trigger: The client begins to mention situations of 'when I first came to counseling' or 'at the beginning', or recalls the initial state fragmentarily.

1223.skill_name: Taking stock of key changes by stage
1223.skill_description: Together with the client, go through the changes that appeared stage by stage in counseling (cognition, emotion, behavior, functioning), record the change points and magnitudes of each stage, and form a panoramic picture of the staged changes.
1223.when_to_use: In the systematic review of the closing session, establishing an overview of changes from initial consultation to each stage.
1223.trigger: When the client mentions changes or milestone progress appearing after different phases, a certain session.

1224.skill_name: Identify and summarize efforts that facilitated change
1224.skill_description: For the changes at each stage, press questions about the specific efforts and practices the client made for them (such as homework, technique application), correspond the changes with their proactive behavior, and highlight their own role and self-efficacy.
1224.when_to_use: After the staged stocktaking, used to connect 'the changes that occurred' with 'the client's concrete actions'.
1224.trigger: When the client describes a change or progress, or explains that a difficulty has been overcome.

1225.skill_name: Reconstruct the timeline and mechanisms of problem improvement
1225.skill_description: Jointly depicting with the client the trajectory of the problem improving along the counseling process, marking key turning points and effective Interventions, clarifying the causal chain of 'how it got better', providing clues for subsequent consolidation and replication.
1225.when_to_use: At the integration and closing stage of the review part, used to summarize stage information into a whole narrative.
1225.trigger: The client can recount multi-stage information and begins to summarize overall changes or ask why they were able to improve.

1226.skill_name: Assign review preparation homework (reviewing counseling notes)
1226.skill_description: Before the formal summary, assigns homework for the client to review counseling notes, review the course, and think about the gains, to increase the completeness and depth of the review and make the summary deeper and more effective.
1226.when_to_use: The preparation period before the closing session, when time permits, used to improve review and summary quality.
1226.trigger: When about to enter the formal summary phase, the client has not yet systematically reviewed the counseling journey or materials are insufficiently prepared.

1250.skill_name: Continuing to apply effective techniques for residual symptoms
1250.skill_description: Based on discussions in the closing phase, guiding the client to continue using techniques verified effective in sessions (such as Exposure techniques), practicing in real situations, until Residual symptoms are eliminated.
1250.when_to_use: At the outlook and unfinished-issues segment of closing counseling, when the client still has some symptoms, needing to develop post-termination self-coping plans and practice paths.
1250.trigger: When the client describes 'still some Anxiety/symptoms occasionally appear', or admits symptoms have not yet fully subsided and asks how to continue handling.

1251.skill_name: Designs and assigns continuous homework until symptoms are eliminated
1251.skill_description: Jointly formulate feasible homework with the client, carrying out repeated practice and recording around the chosen technique, clarifying frequency and context, and prompting them to keep completing it after the end until the residual symptoms disappear.
1251.when_to_use: Used after determining the technique to be used, to turn practice into a concrete action plan, making it easy to keep advancing and consolidating after ending.
1251.trigger: When the client agrees with the methods but lacks specific arrangements, saying 'do not know how to keep practicing' or needing structured task support.

1252.skill_name: Discuss and formulate a self-treatment plan for residual symptoms
1252.skill_description: In the closing session, discuss with the client how to apply the methods learned in counseling to cope with residual problems, clarifying the goals, steps, and responsibilities of self-treatment, enabling them to continue dealing with them independently.
1252.when_to_use: In the summary and outlook stage of the ending session, turns the learned methods into post-ending self-treatment arrangements and execution paths.
1252.trigger: The client acknowledges residual symptoms exist or worries about being unable to cope after ending, proactively asks about follow-up practices or seeks guidance.

1253.skill_name: Guide conducting self-therapy sessions and using standard checklists
1253.skill_description: Encourage the client to regularly conduct self-therapy sessions after ending, following a standard question checklist (such as a thought record form, RET self-help form) to handle residual symptoms and track progress.
1253.when_to_use: In preparation for ending or in the early period after ending, to support the client in independently using tools to handle residual symptoms and carry out continuous self-management.
1253.trigger: The client is willing to do self-help but lacks specific tools or steps, or has already recorded notes and hopes to carry out self-sessions following a checklist.

1246.skill_name: Guiding the client to lead the agenda and homework and autonomously use cognitive techniques
1246.skill_description: Having the client lead the session process as early as possible, including setting agendas on their own, assigning Homework and applying cognitive techniques for Automatic thoughts, gradually reducing counselor participation, enhancing their independent coping ability and confidence, to handle future life problems.
1246.when_to_use: At the 'coping with future life' discussion phase before termination and when regular sessions gradually decrease, for enhancing Independence and preparing for termination.
1246.trigger: The client can already handle problems with less counselor participation, or proactively proposes discussing the agenda and homework arrangements in the session.

1247.skill_name: Attribute progress to the client to reinforce self-efficacy
1247.skill_description: When the client credits treatment progress to the counselor, emphasizing that changes in their own cognitions and behaviors brought success, and summarizing 'changing cognitions and behaviors thus changes emotions', to enhance the client's Self-efficacy and independent coping confidence.
1247.when_to_use: In the review and pre-closing summary stage of each session, used to consolidate gains and enhance independence.
1247.trigger: When the client attributes treatment progress, improvement, or success to the counselor.

1248.skill_name: Emphasize tools' cross-situational availability and promote continued use
1248.skill_description: When teaching cognitive methods and technical tools, clarifying these tools are long-term beneficial for the client, can be applied in present and future various situations, helping them recognize progress at the method level, and prompting them to proactively continue using after termination.
1248.when_to_use: Used when teaching techniques during treatment and expanding gains in the ending stage, to build replicable general coping strategies.
1248.trigger: When teaching cognitive methods or technical tools to the client, or reviewing their learned skills.

1249.skill_name: Guide self-therapy sessions and use standard question lists
1249.skill_description: Encourage the client to conduct self-therapy sessions after regular sessions are reduced and ended, handling problems item by item according to standard question checklists (such as the thought record form, RET self-help form), and keep practicing to maintain and expand coping abilities.
1249.when_to_use: When regular sessions gradually decrease and after termination, for consolidating treatment outcomes and enhancing the ability to independently handle future problems.
1249.trigger: The client reports starting to improve, the regular session frequency decreases, or after termination they need to handle difficulties independently.

1260.skill_name: Using automatic-thought cognitive techniques for new problems
1260.skill_description: In New problems situations, identifying, recording and testing current thoughts with cognitive techniques from the Automatic thoughts phase, distinguishing facts from Interpretations, finding alternative views, transferring methods learned in counseling to new situations by analogy, to reduce bad emotions and guide subsequent coping.
1260.when_to_use: When planning the future in the outlook of closing counseling or Consolidation sessions, or independently facing new life events and challenges after counseling ends, when learned cognitive methods are needed to handle newly emerging thoughts and emotions.
1260.trigger: When the client reports new problems, describing 'do not know what to do' or 'the more I think the worse', or tending to interpret events negatively, hard to think objectively.

1261.skill_name: Designing behavioral experiments to test hypotheses in new problems
1261.skill_description: Regarding the worries or beliefs in the new problem, set up small-scale, low-risk behavioral experiments, clarify the hypothesis to be tested and the observable indicators, carry them out and review the results, correct biased inferences with experience, optimize understanding of the new situation, and improve coping strategies.
1261.when_to_use: When lacking evidence for their own thoughts or expectations in new situations after counseling ends, hard to make decisions, using Behavioral experiments to turn abstract worries into verifiable actions and feedback.
1261.trigger: When the client proposes untested hypotheses or catastrophizing speculations about New problems like 'maybe...' or 'I certainly cannot do it', hard to convince themselves verbally.

1262.skill_name: Develop a behavioral activation plan to advance coping actions
1262.skill_description: Break the new problem down into concrete executable tasks, arrange valuable and attainable activities according to behavioral activation principles, set a timetable and progressive goals, break the stagnation with actual action, obtain a sense of control and positive feedback, and continuously revise the plan to promote resolution.
1262.when_to_use: When New problems need actions to solve, and in the post-termination self-help phase or Consolidation sessions, when structured plans are needed to drive execution and consolidate learned techniques.
1262.trigger: When the client procrastinates facing New problems, lacking action plans or finding it hard to start, self-reporting 'cannot get motivated' or 'always avoiding', leading to stalled progress.

1263.skill_name: Conduct self-therapy sessions to handle new problems
1263.skill_description: After treatment ends, carry out self-therapy sessions according to a standard problem checklist (such as the thought record sheet, self-help sheet), sort out item by item the problems, thoughts and evidence, alternative coping, and action plans, practice independently and review, and with a systematized process transfer the techniques to new situations.
1263.when_to_use: When counseling is gradually reduced or has ended and the client independently encounters new problems, they systematically handle them using the structured framework of the self-therapy session and consolidate self-help ability.
1263.trigger: When the client encounters new difficulties without the therapist's company, hoping to self-handle problems in a step-by-step way rather than immediately seeking others' help.

1264.skill_name: Use Consolidation sessions as backup support
1264.skill_description: Announcing and arranging 1–3 Consolidation sessions after termination (about 3, 6, 12 months). If encountering New problems that cannot be effectively handled, follow-up with the counselor can be scheduled early, reviewing self-help attempts, reinforcing technique application and revising strategies, while relieving the Loneliness and helplessness of facing problems alone.
1264.when_to_use: At the outlook phase of closing counseling to determine follow-up arrangements; later when New problems appear in real life with poor self-help effects, initiating Consolidation sessions to provide support and correction.
1264.trigger: When the client says 'I cannot effectively handle these problems myself' or help-seeking willingness increases, worrying about failing to cope alone, hoping for timely support and guidance.

1367.skill_name: Ongoing thought records and cognitive reappraisal
1367.skill_description: Continuously filling in thought records when mood fluctuates or worsens, recording situation–Automatic thoughts–emotion–behavior, distinguishing subjective speculation from objective facts; challenging irrational beliefs with evidence for/against and alternative Interpretations, and supplementing this session's solutions and effects, gradually reducing residual Anxiety/depression.
1367.when_to_use: During the consolidation phase and when residual Anxiety, depression, sleep distress remain; when mild discomfort remains after treatment or specific situations trigger emotions.
1367.trigger: When Anxiety rises, Low mood, functioning affected or sleep problems; Automatic thoughts like 'being excluded' or 'inferior to others' repeatedly appear and affect emotions.

1377.skill_name: Conducting cognitive exposure and recording thoughts
1377.skill_description: Exposing oneself to uncertain online health information, recording automatic thoughts and problems in practice, encouraging persistence until Anxiety subsides on its own, to weaken unnecessary worries and avoidance.
1377.when_to_use: During the residual phase when facing uncertain, ambiguous health information still triggers Significant anxiety.
1377.trigger: When Anxiety rises encountering vague terms or multiple Interpretations, with urges to continue searching or avoid.

1349.skill_name: Ongoing practice and application of relaxation techniques
1349.skill_description: Practicing relaxation techniques per counseling-learned patterns and applying as needed in daily situations, reducing physiological arousal to relieve Anxiety and insomnia, improving attention and study efficiency; proactively using when emotions easily lose control and can record feelings; when necessary as preparation and consolidation for Systematic desensitization, until Residual symptoms lessen.
1349.when_to_use: During the consolidation and daily maintenance phases; when Residual symptoms like Anxiety, nervousness or poor sleep remain after counseling, or the preparation phase before Systematic desensitization begins.
1349.trigger: Residual physiological or emotional signals such as tension, irritability, palpitations, difficulty falling asleep, and difficulty concentrating.

1368.skill_name: Daily relaxation homework to lower arousal
1368.skill_description: Carry out relaxation training daily as arranged by the homework (such as deep breathing/muscle relaxation), about 20-30 minutes each time, gradually adjusting the duration or frequency; compare before and after practice and record tension and emotional changes. Through stable practice lower overall arousal, until sleep and emotion recover.
1368.when_to_use: When residual Anxiety, nervousness or poor sleep exists; during consolidation for maintaining improvement and tracking symptom changes.
1368.trigger: When Difficulty falling asleep, waking easily, irritability, palpitations or stress physiological reactions have not yet fully subsided.

1456.skill_name: Recording and reviewing to monitor residual symptoms
1456.skill_description: Continuing session homework to record emotions and automatic thoughts, making ABC tables and quantifying emotional intensity and belief levels; tracking the frequency, methods and triggers of impulses/conflicts, identifying high-frequency periods and trigger sources; giving small rewards on conflict-free days, and promptly applying verified effective strategies, observing gradual improvement.
1456.when_to_use: In the maintenance period and daily life when symptoms have improved but still occur occasionally; during daily review or after an event occurs.
1456.trigger: When Anxiety, lowness, Sleep disturbed or study avoidance intermittently appear; multiple mild impulses in a day or emotion rating decreases are not significant; rapidly negativizing the environment.

1393.skill_name: Build the Anxiety hierarchy and set goals
1393.skill_description: Summarizing Anxiety-triggering situations with the client, establishing the Anxiety hierarchy table from low to high by intensity, and setting achievable phase goals for each level, providing a clear route for subsequent gradual desensitization and step-by-step practice, reducing residual Anxiety impact in key scenarios.
1393.when_to_use: When some situations still present Anxiety reactions, needing to plan progressive practice; when preparing to conduct Systematic desensitization after Relaxation training.
1393.trigger: When still tense and avoidant toward specific social/interpersonal/exam scenarios, talking about related topics with obvious unease.

1382.skill_name: Graded exposure according to the hierarchy table
1382.skill_description: Based on the constructed Fear/Social anxiety hierarchy table, progressively conducting imagery desensitization and real exposure from low to high, pairing relaxation responses in relaxed environments, or starting from medium difficulty and advancing gradually, continuing practice until subjective Anxiety drops and target tasks can be stably completed.
1382.when_to_use: When clear Fear or avoidance specific scenarios are not yet fully recovered; entering the exposure practice phase.
1382.trigger: Tense in specific social situations, blushing, palpitations, or always avoiding; when thinking of being rejected or talking, self-rated tension is still high.

1401.skill_name: Identify, test and substitute Automatic thoughts
1401.skill_description: Recording event–Automatic thoughts–emotion–behavior in specific situations, finding supporting and opposing evidence, identifying overgeneralization, perfect Demands and other irrational beliefs, generating more objective and reasonable alternative thoughts, reducing negative emotions and weakening Residual symptoms impact.
1401.when_to_use: Used when residual emotional fluctuation, lowness, or old thoughts reappear; when interpreting events in daily life, to maintain the amount of change.
1401.trigger: When negative beliefs like 'incompetent' or 'being targeted' repeatedly appear with high self-rated credibility, accompanied by Anxiety/irritability; Behavioral avoidance or rumination continues.

1343.skill_name: Quick regulation through breathing and muscle relaxation
1343.skill_description: When Anxiety is triggered or during exposure practice, using brief breathing and segmented muscle relaxation to reduce palpitations and bodily tension, improving control over physiological reactions; after emotions stabilize, reviewing whether irrational thoughts appeared, assisting in relieving Residual symptoms like insomnia and inattention.
1343.when_to_use: During exposure practice or when symptoms are triggered; when stress is high, insomnia or attention is hard to focus.
1343.trigger: When Anxiety physiological reactions like chest tightness, palpitations, rapid breathing, muscle tension, sweaty palms, Difficulty falling asleep, inability to concentrate occur.

1295.skill_name: Mindfulness relaxation practice to improve sleep and mood
1295.skill_description: Arranging fixed practice and temporary use of mindfulness breathing relaxation, focusing on the present moment non-judgmentally noticing breathing and bodily feelings, reducing physiological arousal and rumination; reusing mindfulness and relaxation when Sleep disturbed, and correcting unrealistic expectations with sleep psychoeducation, promoting falling asleep, reducing lowness and crying.
1295.when_to_use: Used in continued practice after introduction; in the after-session self-help stage when sleep or emotional distress, difficulty falling asleep at night, or emotional fluctuation appears.
1295.trigger: When insomnia, early waking or disrupted routines; insufficient energy, Low mood, easily crying when recalling or attention drifting.

1338.skill_name: Guiding self-evaluation and distilling effective strategies
1338.skill_description: Inviting the client to sort key practices that brought improvement, such as recording and self-monitoring, participating in interests and peers, positive imagery, debating irrational beliefs, etc., summarizing gains in their own language, generalizing replicable steps and planning subsequent application, forming a personal insights checklist.
1338.when_to_use: At the ending and consolidation stage or effect evaluation, focusing on the summary of 'what was done that brought progress'; or when entering review and follow-up.
1338.trigger: The client can describe concrete changes and homework gains (such as stabilized emotions, improved sleep, increased social contact, smooth studying), or asks which methods are effective.

1439.skill_description: Review concrete achievements (such as confidence raised, sleep improved, grades risen), affirm their efforts and progress face to face, link them to practice and persistence, encourage expressing insights and reasonable attributions in their own language, consolidating a positive self-concept and continued motivation.
1439.when_to_use: Used at the end of reviewing success or before case closing, to consolidate change and enhance confidence; or when the client self-blames and motivation fluctuates.
1439.trigger: The client reports progress or decreased scale scores, or receives affirming evaluations from others; or expresses doubt and needs clear affirmation.

1414.skill_name: Distilling effective strategies and a technique list
1414.skill_description: Based on case process and homework feedback, sorting effective practices (attention Displacement, time control, family negotiation, Stimulus control, sleep restriction, exercise, belief debate, etc.), generalizing replicable steps and implementation points, pointing to subsequent consolidation and application.
1414.when_to_use: At the summary step of the effect improvement and consolidation stage, or at termination assessment when distilling experience and strategies.
1414.trigger: When the client has shown progress and can describe implemented Interventions and life changes, or asks which methods are most effective.

1315.skill_name: Reinforce successful attribution and arrange practice
1315.skill_description: Centering on positive events and successful cases, ask in detail about the effort and ability they invested, clarify the 'effort — result' link; give affirmation to effective thinking and behavioral practice and name the successful experiences, encourage continued practice and follow-up review, and clarify the focuses to maintain.
1315.when_to_use: In the closing stage of summarizing successful experiences or the 9th-10th consolidation stage, used to consolidate motivation and the practice plan.
1315.trigger: The client reports being praised, notable progress, or willingness to keep practicing, and the source of progress needs verifying and maintenance points formulating.

1460.skill_name: Guiding comparison and listing specific progress
1460.skill_description: With reference to the client's self-assessment, list and compare in one's own language the changes between the initial state and the current state, such as emotional stability, improvement in sleep and interpersonal relations, raised confidence, daring eye contact, and restored functioning, distill the practices and regulation insights that brought about progress, and form an experience checklist.
1460.when_to_use: At the effect consolidation and summary step of sessions 9-10, or at the outcome evaluation and reflection-organizing stage.
1460.trigger: The client is willing to share recent circumstances or can recall specific improvement events, and comparative statements about the initial state and the current state appear in the summary.

1294.skill_name: Affirming change and calibrating realistic expectations
1294.skill_description: Specifically naming efforts and progress in identifying thoughts and Emotion management, giving affirmation and reinforcement, while guiding the establishment of both optimistic and realistic self-expectations, avoiding harsh standards, stabilizing a sustainable change pace, enhancing self-efficacy.
1294.when_to_use: When summarizing reflections, consolidating new behaviors and cognitions and planning subsequent self-requirements.
1294.trigger: When the client demands too much of themselves, goals are vague or expectations for the future waver.

1345.skill_name: Review and package effective methods and techniques
1345.skill_description: Reviewing previous homework and learned techniques, summarizing the most useful methods like thought records, assessing Automatic thoughts, belief correction, behavioral experiments, relaxation, clarifying use situations and gains, listing checklists for continued use in life.
1345.when_to_use: At the consolidation stage or the summary segment before ending, preparing to 'pack up and take away' the effective methods and raise self-help ability.
1345.trigger: When the client has completed multiple Homework and learned various techniques, or asks which methods to continue using in the future.

1400.skill_name: Pointing out directions and plans for continued effort
1400.skill_description: On the basis of review and summary, clarify the points to be consolidated and improved subsequently, put forward concrete directions or suggestions, encourage applying the effective practices to study and life situations, and plan the next steps to maintain the changes and respond to challenges.
1400.when_to_use: The counseling review and summary stage or before the end, used to plan next steps and transfer applications.
1400.trigger: The client asks about next steps or shows continued improvement and willingness to apply what was learned.

1466.skill_name: Distilling takeaways and summarizing a technique list
1466.skill_description: Guide the client to summarize the experience in concise statements (such as 'fear is only an emotion; accepting it, it will pass'), and summarize effective practices and support resources (relaxation training, rational emotive therapy, positive self-suggestion, etc.), recording them as a personalized checklist for easy replication.
1466.when_to_use: After successful exposure or at treatment summary, or during the summary segment of closing and Consolidation sessions.
1466.trigger: When the client completes effective coping or self-reports reduced Anxiety, improved sleep, willing to review and summarize personal insights.

1282.skill_name: Convert insights into self-help strategies and plans
1282.skill_description: Integrating successful insights and life plans into an executable plan, clarifying continued training and follow-up arrangements, confirming feasibility and encouraging implementation; emphasizing skilled use of Automatic thoughts and Behavioral experiments record forms, so as to continue self-regulation and belief verification after leaving counseling.
1282.when_to_use: When developing continuation plans before termination, consolidating new skills and preventing relapse.
1282.trigger: The client proposes a concrete plan and endorses the recording tool as effective, and it is assessed as practically feasible.

1389.skill_name: Affirming growth and emphasizing autonomous efficacy
1389.skill_description: Summarize the role of motivational interviewing, highlight the experience of the client leading the selection and implementation of the change plan, affirm autonomous choice and small-step success, clarify the effort-outcome link, strengthen confidence and the motivation for sustained change, and invite them to self-evaluate progress and gains.
1389.when_to_use: When summarizing successful experiences and maintaining motivation, or psychologically preparing for subsequent self-help and relapse prevention.
1389.trigger: The client's motivation fluctuates, they doubt their autonomy or expect external instruction; concrete gains and growth are presented.

1311.skill_name: Distilling cognitive change and core beliefs
1311.skill_description: Reviewing practices of identifying dysfunctional thoughts and distinguishing subjective speculation/objective facts, summarizing key points of cognitive shifts and emotional improvement, consolidating new core beliefs (lowering expectations, seeing problems from multiple angles, accepting the ordinary self), clarifying applicable situations and possible difficulties for continued practice.
1311.when_to_use: During the consolidation phase or closing summary, when reinforcement of cognitive strategy mastery and transfer is needed.
1311.trigger: When the client can talk about idea changes, recording negative emotional events and distinguishing their sources, or expressing more rational views of outcomes and improved self-acceptance.

1369.skill_name: Name and consolidate personal strengths and efforts
1369.skill_description: Concretize and name strengths and efforts such as arriving on time, strong motivation, taking medication and follow-up as prescribed, and actively participating in practice, summarize their concrete manifestations and practices in counseling, and distill them into sustainable self-management and persistence strategies, as a template for later self-help.
1369.when_to_use: During the consolidation segment, when self-efficacy and behavior maintenance need enhancing; or summarizing the Personal growth phase.
1369.trigger: Records show good adherence and sufficient practice; or the client recognizes her own change and strengths.

1447.skill_name: Affirming growth and encouraging transfer application
1447.skill_description: Review the course from being affirmed to proactively speaking and running for election, strengthen the belief of 'being able to analyze independently and find solutions', give clear affirmation and encouragement, transfer the above strategies to new challenges, and maintain the rhythm and manner of gradual attempts.
1447.when_to_use: The ending stage, when the client prepares to leave the counselor and enter autonomous application.
1447.trigger: The client shows signs of being more independent and self-determined, or multi-party evaluations show positive change.

1472.skill_name: Guiding self-reported takeaways and including others' evaluations
1472.skill_description: Through questioning and listening, prompt the client to summarize in their own language the multidimensional gains and contributing factors, accept others' evaluations (such as being more expressive and livelier), and compare external evidence with self-evaluation, promoting recognition of progress and stable attribution.
1472.when_to_use: At the summary phase of the closing session or Consolidation session, for integrating subjective gains and verifying effectiveness.
1472.trigger: The client reports improvement in mood and behavior, or relays positive evaluations from friends/significant others.

1361.skill_name: Positively affirming and promoting transfer application
1361.skill_description: After emotions and functioning improve, give concretized affirmation and encouragement, point out the effort-gain causal link, guide the extension of positive thinking and cognitive evaluation to other areas of study and life, and strengthen self-efficacy and maintenance of change.
1361.when_to_use: At the end of the Consolidation session summary or the third phase, for consolidating outcomes and preventing relapse.
1361.trigger: When scale scores decrease, the client self-rates as relaxed and calm, others' evaluations show study and work returning to normal, or the client expresses pride and pleasant surprise.

1321.skill_name: Provide suggestions and establish Reflection routines
1321.skill_description: Give specific advice and support regarding study and life, help integrate improvements into the daily rhythm; at the same time form a habit of regular recording and reviewing changes, affirming progress in the log and tracking difficulties and solutions, to consolidate results and prevent relapse.
1321.when_to_use: At the summary and consolidation segment of the last two sessions, or when arranging maintenance and relapse prevention before ending.
1321.trigger: The client is preparing to return to normal life and study, is willing to record and supervise their own changes, or has an existing recording habit that can continue.

1273.skill_name: Pointing out effort directions and setting goals
1273.skill_description: Jointly pointing out subsequent effort directions based on successful experiences (such as self-control, studying hard), setting executable behavioral goals, turning insights into action plans, and encouraging maintaining a positive attitude toward the future, ensuring maintenance and continuous improvement.
1273.when_to_use: When counseling is nearing the end or at follow-up, when a follow-up maintenance and development plan needs forming.
1273.trigger: When outcomes are clear and the client is willing to continue improving, seeking concrete action guidance or expecting encouragement.

1375.skill_name: Distilling and planning application of effective strategies
1375.skill_description: Distilling replicable strategies from effective methods and forming daily application plans, such as limiting search frequency and duration, Relaxation training, attention Displacement, seeking medical/counseling help and positive self-suggestion, clarifying why they work and how to reuse.
1375.when_to_use: At the ending-stage summary and consolidation, when formulating the follow-up self-help and relapse-prevention plan.
1375.trigger: When the client recognizes some methods are effective and willing to continue using in daily life, or asks 'what did I do right'.

1431.skill_name: Connecting techniques to effects, clarifying progress
1431.skill_description: Point-to-point reviewing the correspondence between techniques used and effects, or summarizing effective technique combinations and mechanisms, such as Systematic desensitization combined with relaxation and cognitive techniques gradually weakening Anxiety, clarifying 'which technique works when', to enhance self-efficacy.
1431.when_to_use: Summarizing gains before termination, when 'what brought the change' needs to be clarified or a maintenance strategy formulated.
1431.trigger: When the client reports improved emotions and functioning and can recall specific techniques, or asks about the reasons for progress.

1461.skill_description: Jointly summarizing effective emotion-handling and relaxation methods in this counseling, and practicing in session, emphasizing implementation time periods and conditions for repeated practice, helping reduce Anxiety, improve sleep in daily situations, forming reusable skills.
1461.when_to_use: During the effect Consolidation and termination phase, for turning methods into self-usable tools and training plans.
1461.trigger: When residual emotional distress remains or expressing hope to consolidate coping methods; or able to effectively use relaxation methods and willing to summarize insights.

1443.skill_name: Encouraging transfer application and developing plans
1443.skill_description: Assist in transferring rational cognitive ways and the learned methods to study, interpersonal, and life situations; when encountering similar difficulties, use self-regulation, and formulate a brief persistence plan to maintain change and reduce the possibility of renewed distress.
1443.when_to_use: At the closing summary and outlook stage, or when formulating subsequent consolidation and application plans around the ending.
1443.trigger: When the client expresses a wish to maintain and extend the results, or asks how to apply the learned strategies in more situations.

1415.skill_name: Summarizing growth and giving specific affirmation
1415.skill_description: According to progress in emotions, sleep, study, and interpersonal areas, summarize their growth and give sincere and specific affirmation and praise, highlight the effort-change connection, enhance confidence and self-efficacy, consolidate results, and support the ending transition.
1415.when_to_use: After review and sharing, for the closing summary, highlighting success and growth, reducing separation Anxiety and preparing for termination.
1415.trigger: The client shows obvious progress or test results show symptoms have basically disappeared; or encouragement is needed upon completing homework / a behavioral experiment.

1475.skill_name: Systematically collects the client's self-rated symptom and functioning improvement
1475.skill_description: Based on the client's self-evaluation, structurally summarize changes in sleep, emotion, appetite, attention, study, interpersonal relations, confidence, and attitude, record improvements and remaining distress with concrete life examples and original words, as subjective evidence of the counseling effect and mental health improvement.
1475.when_to_use: At the effect-evaluation stage of counseling termination or consolidation/follow-up visits, used to review the initial and current states from the client's perspective and form a subjective overview of improvement.
1475.trigger: When the client proactively or under Questioning describes recent situations and insights like 'reduced Anxiety, better sleep, improved study efficiency, more harmonious relationships'.

1437.skill_name: Integrate the client's self-report with the counselor's observations and other-ratings to form functional evidence
1437.skill_description: In the effect evaluation stage, comprehensively use the client's self-reported emotional and functional changes, the counselor's on-site observation (such as smoother communication, increased vitality), and feedback from advisors/classmates, verify improvements in study, interpersonal, and life adaptation, and form multi-source, verifiable functional evidence.
1437.when_to_use: At the closing and review stage, when assessment reliability needs to be improved, a comprehensive judgment formed, or follow-up planned.
1437.trigger: The client reports improvement or still having difficulties, while external feedback (from counselors, classmates, etc.) and the counselor's observation cues are available for integration.

1328.skill_name: Quantitatively evaluating improvement against goals and emotion ratings
1328.skill_description: Compare against the emotional goals or self-ratings set initially (such as dropping from 60 to 30, the 0-10 scale), ask the client to report the current score and check the fluctuation and stability, quantify the magnitude and persistence of emotional improvement, as an intuitive basis for effect evaluation.
1328.when_to_use: During the Consolidation session review/effect evaluation phase, or when emotional improvement needs quantifying before termination.
1328.trigger: The client has previously set a specific score or can provide a current emotion self-rating and is willing to compare it with the initial data.

1457.skill_name: The counselor comprehensively assesses and gives consolidation advice
1457.skill_description: The counselor comprehensively evaluating Scales and the client's self-assessment, affirming progress like cognitive correction and core belief changes, pointing out mild Anxiety or perfectionist tendencies and other residuals need not be over-focused, and suggesting continued application of learning in life to improve emotional control and maintain effects.
1457.when_to_use: At the closing of the effect evaluation stage, used to form professional judgments and follow-up application suggestions.
1457.trigger: When overall improvement is marked but mild symptoms or tendencies still exist that need noting and consolidation.

1419.skill_name: Check sleep and physical symptoms and recovery of daily functioning
1419.skill_description: Compare against the initial symptoms, systematically ask about and record the current state of sleep, appetite, physical energy, and study and life functions, verify the degree of improvement and the residual problems, as a basis for risk assessment and subsequent support arrangements.
1419.when_to_use: At the effect evaluation stage or at a return visit, reviewing physical-mental and functional changes at the end of the treatment course.
1419.trigger: The client mentions changes in sleep, appetite, or mental state, or improvement or fluctuation in study and life functioning.

1394.skill_name: Summarize parent and Doctor feedback to verify improvement
1394.skill_description: Combining parents' feedback on communication frequency and attitudes, Doctor's opinions on medication compliance and dosage adjustment, cross-validating psychosomatic recovery and risk levels, supplementing the blind spots of the client's self-report, improving effect evaluation.
1394.when_to_use: When the assessment phase needs corroboration of improvement or identifying residual risks, or when planning to adjust follow-up arrangements.
1394.trigger: When parents or Doctor provide phased feedback, medication plans change or there are differing opinions on recovery.

1440.skill_name: Invite the client to self-rate recent status with examples
1440.skill_description: Guide the client to narrate, with concrete life segments, recent emotions, somatic symptoms, interpersonal and study adaptation, list key changes and examples compared with the first visit, forming a subjective assessment of the current state, as material for subsequent checking and summary.
1440.when_to_use: At the start of effect evaluation in the Consolidation session review segment, prioritizing collecting subjective experiences and recent conditions.
1440.trigger: When the client starts self-reporting recent conditions like 'recent mood is good' or 'no headaches', or is willing to review changes.

1350.skill_name: Compare emotional self-ratings pre-post and quantify change
1350.skill_description: Invite the client to self-evaluate the current emotional state on 0-10 segments and compare with the initial visit score, clarify the extent of improvement and the difference in felt body sensation, and record it in writing as a basis for quantitative evaluation, corroborating each other with the subjective narration.
1350.when_to_use: During Consolidation session review evaluation or before termination, when emotional improvement needs quantifying.
1350.trigger: The client can recall the initial-visit scores, or reports that their emotions have clearly improved or still fluctuate, and is willing to conduct a self-assessment.

1459.skill_name: Comprehensively assess and point out residual issues and risks
1459.skill_description: Integrating Scales, client reports and observations, clarifying achieved changes and not-yet-complete areas (such as compulsion, interpersonal sensitivity still existing), marking residual risks and areas needing consolidation, and giving 'needs later counseling and consolidation' prompts.
1459.when_to_use: At the efficacy evaluation summary closing, before preparing termination and later arrangements.
1459.trigger: When retesting shows there are still problem factors, or the client still reports related distress and the residue and follow-up arrangements need to be explained.

1362.skill_description: In subsequent follow-ups and tracking, verifying goal achievement, integrating assessment scores, self and others' ratings, judging whether bad emotions have improved and whether they can focus on exam preparation or maintain functioning, forming a comprehensive effect conclusion.
1362.when_to_use: After counseling ends or in the follow-up stage, used to confirm treatment-effect maintenance and consolidation outcomes.
1362.trigger: Entering follow-up / tracking arrangements, when a professional evaluation conclusion about counseling attainment needs to be formed.

1384.skill_name: Comparing goal attainment and core symptom indicator changes
1384.skill_description: Around key indicators such as crying frequency, attention concentration, emotional relief, relationships with family, and study and life states, compare the first visit with current performance, quantify and record changes, and judge the achievement of near-term and long-term goals.
1384.when_to_use: At the counseling effect evaluation part, when goal achievement and core indicator changes need quantifying.
1384.trigger: When the client reports specific improvement clues like 'almost no longer crying' or 'can concentrate attention'.

1323.skill_name: Records improvements in emotion and interpersonal functioning observed by the counselor
1323.skill_description: Summarize the professional observations in subsequent sessions, record changes such as the client's emotional stability, increased pleasantness, and enhanced interpersonal skills, comprehensively evaluate progress and recovery from the functional perspective, and supplement the chain of subjective and objective evidence.
1323.when_to_use: During the consolidation phase's consecutive sessions and closing summary.
1323.trigger: Signs observed in sessions that the client is more stable, interacts more naturally, and actively integrates into the group.

1411.skill_name: Collect feedback from significant others observing functional improvement
1411.skill_description: On the premise of obtaining consent, learn from the advisor, teachers, or classmates about the client's emotions, study and life arrangements, social recovery, and other external observations, cross-validating the improvement and adaptation from a third-party perspective.
1411.when_to_use: During a comprehensive assessment before case closure or follow-up, when an external perspective is needed to verify functional improvement.
1411.trigger: The client agrees to contact significant others or has established a communication channel with the school counselor.

1454.skill_name: Evaluate attempt effectiveness based on homework feedback
1454.skill_description: Review and discuss the approaches the client listed for improving getting along with classmates and the results of recent attempts, confirm the peer responses and emotional changes obtained, and evaluate the actual effect and sustainability, as evidential-basis proof of functional improvement.
1454.when_to_use: The homework review and consolidation assessment phase before counseling ends.
1454.trigger: When the client submits an action plan or reports interaction attempts already made and specific feedback.

1327.skill_name: Summarize Client self-assessment on skill application and functional improvement
1327.skill_description: Organizing the client's self-reported gains and application evidence: such as frequently applying mindfulness, TIP, ACCEPTS and interpersonal skills (GIVE, FAST), as well as functional improvements like returning to school, improved relationships with Father and classmates, as a basis for subjective efficacy and transferable ability.
1327.when_to_use: During the effect evaluation and review phase, for taking stock of gains and skill application from the client's perspective.
1327.trigger: When the client proactively mentions daily application of learned strategies and life, and Interpersonal relationships have improved significantly.

1356.skill_name: Guide the client to self-rate and report others' feedback
1356.skill_description: Guide the client to evaluate in their own words changes in confidence, mood, interpersonal relations, and so on, and to relay the changes observed by those around them, incorporating them into the subjective outcome indicators, cross-validating with objective measurements, and completing the comprehensive assessment.
1356.when_to_use: At the effect evaluation and review stage, when preparing to integrate subjective and objective evidence.
1356.trigger: The client begins self-assessment or proactively mentions feedback from friends/classmates about their changes.

1354.skill_name: Assess concrete improvements in functioning and life adaptation
1354.skill_description: Review specific manifestations such as sleep improving, a regular schedule, participation in part-time work/investment in study, as indicators of improvement in mental health and social function, assisting in forming a comprehensive assessment of the degree of recovery.
1354.when_to_use: During the review session of the Consolidation and termination phase, for judging functional recovery and life adaptation improvement.
1354.trigger: The client reports recent improvements in routine, better sleep, starting part-time work, or engagement in study and work.

1416.skill_name: Guide the client to state subjective changes and review Anxiety levels
1416.skill_description: Around symptoms, focus, cognition, relationships and activity participation, inviting the client to describe changes and the decline or fluctuation of Anxiety intensity/frequency with specific examples, recording subjective feelings as direct indicators of mental health improvement.
1416.when_to_use: During the Consolidation session review phase, conducting effect evaluation, comparing initial assessment with current subjective feelings.
1416.trigger: When the client says 'Anxiety reduced/can focus more', etc.; or proactively asks whether their changes are significant.

1428.skill_name: Making efficacy judgments integrating clinical observation and testing
1428.skill_description: Combining the counselor's session observations (mental state, facial expressions, Interpersonal relationships improvement) with re-tested Scale results, judging whether recent goals are achieved, and clarifying follow-up suggestions like 'still needs further observation'.
1428.when_to_use: During the effect summary of Consolidation sessions and the pre-termination evaluation segment.
1428.trigger: When observing improved mental state, decreased Scale scores or signs of Interpersonal relationships improvement.

1470.skill_name: Forming and feeding back comprehensive assessment conclusions
1470.skill_description: Comprehensively evaluating self-ratings, others' ratings and Scale results, clarifying Anxiety relief, goal achievement and functional improvement degree, and feeding back evaluation conclusions to the client in plain language, as a basis for termination and follow-up arrangements.
1470.when_to_use: Before the ending decision, when an overall effect judgment needs forming and feedback to the client is needed.
1470.trigger: Re-measurement has been completed and self- and other-evaluations collected; materials show symptom relief and functional improvement.

1335.skill_name: Conducting the counselor's comprehensive evaluation against counseling goals
1335.skill_description: Using established recent goals as reference, comprehensively evaluating client reports and session observations, judging the degree of depression relief, mental outlook improvement and irrational beliefs being replaced by rational beliefs, forming professional conclusions and recording.
1335.when_to_use: After collecting self-evaluation and objective information, when it is necessary to compare with goals to form a professional judgment.
1335.trigger: Short-term goals have been clarified and clues of improvement/residuals collected, and the degree of achievement needs to be summarized.

1427.skill_name: Collects external evaluations from family and colleagues to verify functional improvement
1427.skill_description: Ask about and record observations by family members or colleagues on the client's changes, such as going out for entertainment more, increased willingness to communicate, making friends at the company, and so on, in order to verify improvements in social functioning and interpersonal relations and supplement the evaluation evidence.
1427.when_to_use: When conducting counseling outcome evaluation, needing external corroboration of social functioning change.
1427.trigger: The client mentions feedback from family or colleagues, or family members' reflections on life changes can be obtained.

1409.skill_name: Review trigger situation performance to identify Residual symptoms
1409.skill_description: Focusing on specific scenarios of recent interactions with trigger objects, assessing whether tension remains, whether Anxiety is significantly relieved and whether communication is basically normal, locating Residual symptoms and high-trigger situations, providing a basis for subsequent self-regulation and follow-up.
1409.when_to_use: When reviewing counseling effects, discussing coping performance and residual reactions in typical trigger situations.
1409.trigger: When the client reports recent experiences of conversing or encountering trigger objects and mentions tension or bodily reactions.

1388.skill_name: Identify Residual symptoms and relapse signs and develop monitoring points
1388.skill_description: Based on client feedback, identifying remaining symptoms and high-risk situations, discussing early warning signals and feasible countermeasures, forming monitoring points for relapse prevention and follow-up, marking areas needing consolidation.
1388.when_to_use: The risk inventory and relapse prevention planning segment before ending preparation and follow-up.
1388.trigger: When the client still has residual Anxiety or worries about recurrence, or reports specific triggering cues and emotional fluctuations.

1283.skill_name: Re-administer and compare symptom self-rating scale scores
1283.skill_description: In the counseling termination phase, re-testing depression/Anxiety and other symptom self-rating Scales, comparing item by item with initial test data, recording score and level changes, quantifying the magnitude of emotional Symptom improvement and residual degree, as objective basis.
1283.when_to_use: When termination evaluation and Consolidation sessions need quantified efficacy or verification of subjective improvement.
1283.trigger: When pre/post-test data are available or objective quantitative evidence is needed.

1448.skill_name: Follow up to collect the client's self-assessment information and functional performance
1448.skill_description: Conduct follow-up after counseling ends, around life indicators such as sleep, emotions, interpersonal and parent-child contact, study and socializing, invite the client to describe their current situation with concrete examples, forming self-evaluation data to measure improvement and maintenance.
1448.when_to_use: During Consolidation sessions after counseling ends or 1-month follow-ups, for systematically assessing changes and stability.
1448.trigger: When the client proactively reports specific recent conditions in follow-ups like 'sleep is much better but occasional insomnia' or 'weekly calls with Mother'.

1358.skill_name: Uses specific social behavior indicators to assess social functioning recovery
1358.skill_description: Centering on classroom and peer scenes, check positive behavior indicators: proactively listening to the teacher speak, making eye contact with the teacher, raising a hand to signal, a louder voice, proactively approaching and cooperatively playing, helping peers, etc., assessing social functioning and adaptation improvement with behavioral indicators.
1358.when_to_use: At the end of the treatment course or in consolidation sessions, when it is necessary to assess life adaptation and social functioning improvement.
1358.trigger: When the client or family reports specific changes and examples in school and peer interactions.

1336.skill_name: Collect peer evaluations to corroborate functional improvement
1336.skill_description: Collect feedback from classmates on changes in communication, participation in collective activities, speaking in class, learning efficiency, and so on, as external evidence of recovery in social functioning, cross-checking the client's self-ratings against the counselor's observations.
1336.when_to_use: At effect evaluation, used to verify social functioning improvement and behavior change.
1336.trigger: Classmates or significant others can provide concrete feedback on classroom participation, communication and learning performance.

1404.skill_name: Guide reporting of life-functioning and adaptation changes
1404.skill_description: Inviting the client to talk about insights and real-life changes, such as being more themselves communicating with Mother, more relaxed relationships, ignoring physiological discomfort, body trembling no longer occurring, to assess life adaptation and functional improvement with specific examples.
1404.when_to_use: During the outcome evaluation in the consolidation stage, when supplementing functional evidence after scale comparisons.
1404.trigger: The client proactively describes subjective improvements such as 'feeling relaxed', 'able to be myself' and gives examples of changes in life and physiological symptoms.

1357.skill_name: Clinical observation comparing cognitive, emotional, and behavioral changes
1357.skill_description: Based on verbal, emotional, and behavioral cues in the session, compare changes before and after in cognition and self-view, emotional stability, and frequency of obsessive thinking, forming the counselor's professional assessment conclusion and supplementing evidence beyond quantitative indicators.
1357.when_to_use: At each session summary and termination assessment, combining scales and self-evaluation for a comprehensive judgment.
1357.trigger: When visible emotional improvement in session, or the client states no longer being troubled by strange looks, reduced obsessive thoughts.

1279.skill_name: Follow-up visits and observation to verify improvement and goal attainment
1279.skill_description: Through interview observation and follow-up, checking goal achievement and functional improvement, such as enhanced confidence, being able to normally face exams and employment, accepting rank changes, judging whether expectations are met and recording conclusions.
1279.when_to_use: In the consolidation stage and follow-up, used to objectively assess treatment effects and social functioning recovery.
1279.trigger: The client appears calm and cooperative in the interview, or reports being able to face real tasks such as exams and employment calmly.

1444.skill_name: Integrates others' evaluations and study-functioning data to verify improvement
